AT A GLANCE

* Carlos P. Romulo was incorrectly claimed to be a representative of the Philippines at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944.
* The actual Philippine delegates were Andres Soriano, Jaime Hernandez, Joseph Foley, and Ismael Mathay, with Romulo not being among them.
* The claim was fact-checked due to its widespread circulation on social media, with the video reaching over 829,000 views.

##### At a glance:

* Claim: Carlos P. Romulo represented the Philippines in the Bretton Woods Conference that took place in 1944.
* Rating: FALSE
* The facts: Romulo was not among the representatives to the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944. The Philippine delegates were Andres Soriano, Jaime Hernandez, Joseph Foley, and Ismael Mathay.
* Why we fact-checked this: As of writing, the video containing this post had been viewed 829,000 times, and the post has 39,000 reactions, 2,500 comments, and 31,000 shares.

##### Complete details:

Facebook page “Ophir” posted a video on March 15 that said Carlos P. Romulo was a Philippine representative to the Bretton Woods Conference held in New Hampshire in 1944.

The video said: “Bakit ipapahiram ang mga ginto sa ibang bansa? Simple lang. Sa desisyong nabuo sa Bretton Woods Conference of 1944 na ginanap sa New Hampshire, USA, na dinaluhan ng 44 countries kasama ang Pilipinas (represented by Carlos P. Romulo)…”

(Why would other countries be loaned gold? It’s simple. In the decision formed by Bretton Woods Conference of 1944 that took place in New Hampshire, USA, which was attended by 44 countries including the Philippines [represented by Carlos P. Romulo]…)

As of writing, the video has been viewed over 829,000 times, and has 44,000 reactions, 2,800 comments, and 34,000 shares.

Another Facebook page, “Filipino Future,” made the same claim about Romulo in two Facebook posts on January 17 and September 5, 2020. As of writing, these two posts have a total of at least 7,200 reactions, 954 comments, and about 5,500 shares.

The claim is false.

An entry in the Official Gazette titled “The President’s Day: June 27, 1944” said that former president Manuel Quezon named the following as the Philippine delegates to the Bretton Woods Conference:

* Hon. Andres Soriano, secretary of finance (chairman of the delegation)
* Hon. Jaime Hernandez, auditor-general
* Mr. Joseph Foley, manager of the Philippine National Bank, N. Y. Agency
* Mr. Ismael Mathay, technical assistant to the auditor-general (secretary to the delegation)

Carlos P. Romulo was not among the names that Quezon mentioned.

The Bretton Woods Conference was formally named the United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference, which took place from July 1 to 22, 1944, in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, United States.

Volume 1 of the US Department of State publication “PROCEEDINGS AND DOCUMENTS OF THE United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference” also listed Soriano, Hernandez, Foley, and Mathay as the Philippine attendees to the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference. Volume 2 did not mention Mathay but listed down the other 3. Romulo’s name was not mentioned in either volume.

In the financial history paper “Who Was at Bretton Woods?” on the website of the Center for Financial Stability, the authors Kurt Schuler and Mark Bernkopf said that they are offering “for the first time a nearly complete list” of the attendees to the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference. # Newly Updated Inventory Lists in Online Exhibits

The World Bank Group Archives regularly publishes online exhibits on interesting topics in the institution’s history. In some cases, inventory lists containing archival records relevant to the topic are included. These lists can help researchers who want to dig deeper into our history by accessing archival records. In cases where the material has been declassified and digitized, links to these records are also provided in the inventory lists. Recently, the Archives updated the lists in the following exhibits to reflect the latest information about disclosure status and to include links to newly digitized records.

---

* A Bold Vision to Defeat River Blindness

  The World Bank Group’s first foray into the health sector was one of its most successful.
* In 1958, India was threatened by a balance of payments crisis midway through its Second Five-Year Development Plan. The Indian government requested the World Bank Group to organize additional financial support.
* The World Bank's Role as Mediator in the 1950s

  A small number of prominent Bank-led mediation efforts in the 1950s illustrate how the World Bank extended itself beyond loans to facilitate economic development.
* Bretton Woods and the Birth of the World Bank

  On July 1, 1944, delegates from 44 nations met at the secluded Mount Washington Hotel in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire to participate in what became known as the Bretton Woods Conference.

---

---

---

Check out other exhibits authored by the World Bank Group Archives. These exhibits, which range in topic from historic firsts to impactful personalities and whimsical reflections, help illuminate the rich history of the institution. In each exhibit, you will find archival records and photographs selected from our holdings.

---

# World Bank Group Archives

The Archives preserves the institutional memory of the World Bank Group and provides public access to records of the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA).

About Us

* Discovery Tool

  To mark the 80th anniversary of the first Annual Meetings in September 1946, the Archives has created a timeline highlighting the 28 Annual Meetings held in member countries outside Washington, DC. featuring archival records, photos, a/v, and more!
* Exhibit

  To mark the thirtieth anniversary of James D. Wolfensohn’s arrival as president of the World Bank Group, the Archives launched a series of product releases and events, including an exhibit at our headquarters in Washington, DC. Explore a virtual reality version of the exhibit featuring archival records, audiovisual materials, and more!
* Finding Aids

  ## New descriptions published on Archives Catalog

  The World Bank Group Archives regularly publishes new series-level archival descriptions on its Archives Catalog. These descriptions inform Access to Information requests by external researchers and facilitate access to digitized records. Check out our newest releases, including the urban development sector and two former managing directors.
* The WBG Archives is launching a series of product releases and events to celebrate President Wolfensohn’s legacy and to draw attention and facilitate access to records from his presidency.
* Finding Aids

  ## Newly Updated Inventory Lists in Online Exhibits

  The Archives regularly publishes online exhibits on topics from the institution’s history. Inventory lists containing relevant archival records and links to digitized records are included for some of these exhibits. The Archives has recently updated the lists for these exhibits.
* Exhibit

  In recognition of Black History Month, this World Bank Group Archives exhibit illuminates what we have learned from the documentary evidence in our holdings, and presents the inspiring people, programs, and perspectives related to the WBG's ongoing commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion.

## World Bank Group Historical Timeline

The timeline offers an engaging way to learn about the important moments in the history of the World Bank while discovering the gems of the World Bank Group Archives.

## Flagship Discovery Tools

The Archives Catalog contains archival descriptions and provides access to digitized records.

The Multimedia Catalog provides access to thousands of photos and recordings documenting World Bank operations, presidents, official signings, and more.

The Oral History Program website contains transcripts, summaries, and audio clips of interviews with former World Bank staff.

Track World Bank membership over time and access historical profiles for every member country.

## Archives Spotlight

Exhibit

On July 1, 1944, delegates from forty-four nations met in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire to agree on a new system of international cooperation. Learn more about this historic meeting and view archival records, audiovisual materials, and more.

website

The Web Archives provides access to World Bank websites that have been discontinued or significantly updated. Archived sites date from 1998 to the present.

Video

This short promotional video describes the possibilities available to researchers when they “jump in and explore” the holdings of the World Bank Group Archives.
